FDA inspectors also highlighted shortcomings in Alkem’s response to customer complaints. The company has received about 38 complaints for broken and wet tablets distributed to the U.S. since September 2025. The name of the tablets is again redacted in the warning letter. Alkem identified mechanical stress during transport, compounded by excessive headspace in the bottle, as the root cause of the problem.
In response, the company took steps to protect tablets from breakage and moisture uptake. However, Alkem continued to receive complaints of broken tablets after implementing the changes. During the FDA’s inspection, the company committed to suspending production of the tablets, but it continued to distribute previously manufactured lots and failed to send a field action report to the FDA.
Another part of the warning letter addresses Alkem’s oversight of its equipment maintenance program. The FDA accused Alkem of reporting machine parts as damaged and removing them for destruction without having an adequate system to assess the quality and safety of drug products manufactured using the unsuitable equipment.
Inspectors also observed that equipment cleaned and stored on March 27 had rust-like discoloration on April 20. The FDA interpreted the discoloration as evidence of inadequate post-cleaning inspection and a failure to maintain equipment in a suitable state.
The FDA has advised Alkem to engage a consultant to help it meet manufacturing requirements. The agency may withhold approval of new applications or supplements listing Alkem as a drug manufacturer until violations are completely addressed.

I gotta tell you, this is not a bad way to spend $55,500! Plus a buyer's fee, of course. What we have here is a relatively low-mileage Stingray that's been very well looked-after, according to the original owner who bought the car for $85,150 roughly six years ago. They only drove it 4,000 miles before deciding to auction it off.
The highest bidder did a great job to come in at $30,000 below MSRP, so we can strike this up as a massive win for the buyer, but a considerable loss for the seller. I know it's a 2020 model year car, but again, you have to look at the variables, and everything points to this thing being in tip top shape.
"Congratulations. You are basically getting a new car. It's never been abused and it hasn't ever even been driven in the rain," stated the original owner in the ad's comments section.
And I'll tell you something else - I don't even mind the Torch Red, which is far from my favorite C8 Vette color. But it really suits this Stingray, especially with those black 19" and 20" alloy wheels. It's a healthy contrast. Other interesting bits include the removable roof panel, LED headlights, the rear spoiler, quad exhaust outlets, the Michelin tires, and so on.
This car was also fitted with a front-axle lift system, Magnetic Selective Ride Control, plus the Z51 Performance Package, which added the revised suspension and the red Z51-branded Brembo calipers.
Meanwhile, interior highlights include the Adrenaline Red leather power-adjustable seats (also heated and ventilated), an 8" touchscreen infotainment system, a 14-speaker Bose sound system, dual-zone automatic climate control, cruise control, a head-up display, a heated and leather-wrapped steering wheel, and the likes of rear-cross traffic alert and blind-spot monitoring to keep you safe.
As for performance, the 6.2-liter LT2 V8 engine is pushing 495 horsepower and 470 lb-ft of torque to the rear wheels via a Tremec eight-speed dual-clutch automatic and a limited-slip differential. On a drag-prepped surface, you might even be able to hit 60 mph (97 kph) in 2.9 seconds, but in daily traffic you're not getting anywhere near those numbers. Expect more like... 3.5 seconds. Which still isn't bad at all.

It sold for $53,500 - just a couple of grand less than this Torch Red example. I don't think there's anything left to say. Absolutely stolen, this thing was! Personally, I wouldn't even complain it's not a Z06 given the massive "discount."
If you're on a tighter budget, the only thing better than a $95,000 used Z06 is a $55,000 Stingray. How can you go wrong?

Amgen and Bristol Myers Squibb have reached a settlement over PD-1 drug Opdivo, allowing biosimilar entry to the market in 2028.
A settlement has cleared the way for Amgen to launch a biosimilar of Bristol Myers Squibb’s immunotherapy drug Opdivo in 2028, a legal development that provides investors with clarity as the blockbuster medicine heads toward its patent cliff.
The agreement marks the first of many to come for the PD-1 class of drugs, which changed cancer treatment for the better and brought in billions in sales for drugmakers. Leading the class is Keytruda, for which Merck has yet to announce a biosimilar settlement, analysts from BMO Capital Markets pointed out on Wednesday.
Amgen plans to launch ABP 206 in the U.S. on Oct. 1, 2028 pending approval from the FDA, according to a Tuesday press release . A biologics license application has already been submitted and accepted by the agency, with a decision expected by the end of the year. Sandoz, as well as partners Intas and Xbrane, have Opdivo biosimilar candidates in development as well.
BMO sees the biosimilar launches weighing on BMS in 2029, when revenue for Opdivo will plummet 22% year over year. The firm expects the drug to collect $11.6 billion in 2028, dropping to $3.7 billion by 2031. BMS, therefore, needs to make some moves to shore up earnings in the years to come.
“While not explicitly confirmed, we see this settlement and recent management changes as potential signals prepping for larger-scale BD,” BMO wrote.

BMO Capital Markets is more impressed by Merck’s plans to replace lost Keytruda revenue than on Bristol Myers Squibb’s efforts to fill the expected void that will come from loss of exclusivity for both Opdivo and Eliquis.

On Tuesday, BMS announced that CFO David Elkins is departing, to be replaced by Kevin Dillon. Earlier this month, the company re - organized its R&D department and announced that Chief Research Officer Robert Plenge would leave by the end of the year.
All of these actions are “internal housekeeping ahead of effectuating a transaction,” according to BMO.
BMS leadership has not been shy about the desire for a deal, with Leerink Partners noting in October that the company has high debt but still some flexibility to conduct a transaction.
The company was rumored to be an acquisition target of AstraZeneca in August. The dramatic deal could have helped BMS prepare for its upcoming loss of exclusivity for key products like Opdivo and the Pfizer-partnered blood thinner Eliquis, analysts said at the time. Those two drugs accounted for half of BMS’ revenue in 2025. But that mega-merger never came to fruition.
Investors are waiting for a number of upcoming clinical catalysts for BMS, including Phase 3 data for the oral Factor XIa inhibitor milvexian in secondary stroke prevention that is due by the end of the year . A separate late-stage trial for acute coronary syndrome was halted after investigators determined the Johnson & Johnson-partnered medicine was unlikely to meet its goal.
Another milvexian readout for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation, which BMO called “the biggie,” will follow in 2027. The firm warned investors to “buckle up” for some share volatility from BMS over the coming months.
“We view the next six months of BMY transformative to the story, either solidifying the next legs of P&L [profit & loss] growth or forcing management back the drawing board to chart the next course,” BMO wrote.

Maersk has warned customers of continued disruption across its UK and Ireland logistics network, as high import volumes and a combination of port and inland transport bottlenecks hamper efforts to clear cargo backlogs.
In a customer advisory yesterday, the Danish carrier said sustained high import volumes, vessel schedule delays, adverse weather and recent rail disruptions had put pressure on both port and landside operations across its UK and Ireland network.
“While services are recovering, existing backlogs and high inland storage use mean it will take time for normal network fluidity to return,” it said.
“As these pressures are interconnected, disruption in one part of the network can create knock-on effects elsewhere.”
Maersk assured customers it was reviewing vessel and cargo plans, deploying alternative routes and inland transport solutions where appropriate, and facilitating the movement of empty containers.
It urged shippers to collect import boxes promptly and check empty-container return instructions before dispatching trucks.
According to Kuehne+Nagel’s latest weekly port operational update, London Gateway was recording average vessel waiting times of two days, despite dry and reefer yard occupancy having eased to 75% and 58%, respectively.
High laden container density continues to hamper productivity, while a four-hour IT outage on 19 November halted operations and resulted in numerous rail service failures. Berth restrictions are expected to remain in place until mid-December.
Meanwhile, at Southampton, vessel waiting times averaged 1.5 days and berth windows were moving closer to pro forma schedules, although the port remained reluctant to accommodate ad hoc calls amid wider UK congestion.
And across the Channel, congestion at several major North European terminals continues to threaten schedule recovery.
Meanwhile, Hamburg’s CTH terminal was operating at 99% yard occupancy, with reefer capacity already exceeded and further discharge-heavy vessel calls expected to exacerbate the situation.
At Bremerhaven, where yard occupancy stood at 89%, the diversion of some 1,000 boxes originally destined for Wilhelmshaven was adding to capacity pressure.
K+N said there was “no meaningful schedule recovery currently visible” at Wilhelmshaven, with accumulated delays, adverse weather and late vessel arrivals continuing to disrupt operations.
However, there has been some respite at Antwerp and Le Havre, where yard occupancy has improved.
In Asia, Japanese gateways are experiencing particularly acute yard congestion, with utilisation at three Tokyo terminals ranging between 107% and 120%, while labour shortages are compounding productivity issues at Yokohama.
Yard utilisation at terminals in Port Klang and Vietnam’s Cai Mep also remained above 90%, while renewed carrier demand was putting pressure on operations at Singapore.
And in Australia, carriers have begun omitting calls at Sydney in response to ongoing congestion, K+N reported.
However, some of the longest vessel queues were recorded in Africa, with Mozambique’s Beira seeing average waiting times of more than 13 days, owing to weather disruption and slow inland cargo evacuation, while vessels calling at Ghana’s Tema faced waits of around 5.4 days.
Landside bottlenecks are also evident in the US, where average rail dwell times have reached 13 days at Miami, 11 at Long Beach and 10 at Los Angeles, according to the forwarder.

The Bugatti Chiron's Replacement Could Have Been an Electric SUV, Claims Mate Rimac
61 photos
Photo: Bugatti
The Chiron is best viewed as the Veyron with many improvements over the Piech-era hypercar. Its successor, however, could have been an electric sport utility with four seats instead of a two-seat hypercar with a Cosworth-built naturally aspirated V16 and three electric motors for good measure. According to Mate Rimac, Volkswagen proposed the electric SUV route back in 2020.
At the time, the Croatian outfit headed by Mate was brought in to work on the electric powertrain. The group's idea ultimately ran into a problem that had nothing to do with performance credentials. Bugatti needed an entirely new platform for such a vehicle, and the cost of developing one for Bugatti made the business case unworkable. Indeed, the group did not consider the Premium Platform Electric used by Porsche, Bentley, and the Audi brand.
Given the aforementioned, the project never properly got underway. What followed was far more consequential. Speaking to Classic Driver, the man in charge of Bugatti today made it clear that Volkswagen's proposed zero-emission sport utility vehicle would have borrowed a few bits and pieces from the Rimac Nevera. The Croatian automaker already had experience in this regard, and reworking all that hardware for Bugatti was part of the plan.
Thinking about it, a four-seat SUV with all-electric propulsion would have required a completely different approach to packaging, aero, chassis engineering, and cooling from an electric hypercar like the Nevera. While it could have been exceptionally fast, such a vehicle would have answered a different question about what a Bugatti was supposed to be.
Photo: Bugatti The project's failure is rooted in the Wolfsburg-based parent company's platform strategy. The Volkswagen Group spreads development costs across a bunch of models and brands, but the peeps at Bugatti had completely different requirements from everything available at the time. Mate claims Rimac couldn't simply borrow an existing Volkswagen Group architecture.
Mate then proposed that Rimac develop the next Bugatti, leaving the group responsible for selling it. He likened the arrangement to Magna Steyr, namely the contract manufacturer that builds the Mercedes G-Class and other vehicles for a bunch of automakers. Examples also include the Toyota GR Supra coupe and its BMW-badged twin, the G29-series Z4 roadster.
In other words, Rimac would have become a specialist development and manufacturing partner for the group-controlled Bugatti marque. Later on, a group executive proposed Rimac taking over Bugatti. Mate originally thought the suggestion was a joke, but said executive was dead serious. Back in July 2021, the Porsche division and Rimac announced a joint venture dubbed Bugatti Rimac, with Rimac's side holding 55 percent.
Photo: Bugatti At the time, Mate pushed for a hybrid with a distinct internal combustion engine from the quad-turbo W16 of the Chiron and Veyron before it. Rimac paid Cosworth a bunch of money to begin developing the resulting V16 before Rimac had completed the deal to take over Bugatti, using a four-pot mill to evaluate its design. Lest we forget, the Aston Martin Valkyrie's Cosworth V12 started as a quarter-size test mule with three pots.
The Classic Driver Talks episode further includes a segment where Mate talks about a three-month Panamera battery project, which helped win Porsche over. Rimac was given three months to demonstrate an improvement, yet the resulting battery doubled the Panamera's electric range within the very same space while not adding a single kilogram over the factory unit.
Another segment worth your time sees Mate talk about the Nevera's commercial shortfall. The TL;DR version is that straight-line performance and Nurburgring lap times no longer provide enough distinction at the top of the automotive market, and that's coming from the guy who built Rimac's reputation on electric hypercars. Only 71 units of the Nevera have been sold, and production is wrapping up by the end of 2026 with no successor in sight.

The latest FreightWaves Freight Distress Report points to continued workforce reductions across trucking, third-party logistics, truck manufacturing, packaging and consumer goods production as the U.S. enters the holiday season .
Nine companies have announced workforce reductions affecting up to 7,656 workers, including Procter & Gamble’s long-term plan to eliminate as many as 7,000 manufacturing and logistics jobs. The remaining eight companies account for 656 job cuts tied to facility closures and contract losses.
The latest round of layoffs comes during what is traditionally one of the busiest periods of the year for retailers, trucking companies and distribution networks.
Procter & Gamble targets up to 7,000 supply chain jobs
Consumer goods giant Procter & Gamble Co. (NYSE: PG ) plans to reduce its manufacturing and logistics workforce by 20% to 30%, potentially eliminating as many as 7,000 positions by the end of the decade.
The reductions are part of a broader productivity initiative aimed at generating up to $10 billion in cumulative savings from fiscal 2027 through fiscal 2030.
The initiative includes an increased emphasis on automation, reflecting a broader shift among manufacturers toward technology-driven supply chain operations.
The planned reductions represent a longer-term restructuring rather than an immediate mass layoff.
Walgreens contract loss costs 66 truck drivers their jobs
CPC Special Logistics East LLC, a trucking contractor for Walgreens, expects to permanently lay off 69 employees in Connecticut after the retailer decided not to renew its contract.
In a Nov. 23 notice filed with the Connecticut Department of Labor, CPC said operations at Walgreens’ distribution center at 80 International Drive in Windsor and associated driver locations are expected to end around Jan. 30.
The affected employees include 66 commercial truck drivers, a regional manager, a safety manager and an administrative assistant.
The notice was issued three days before Thanksgiving.
Saddle Creek, GEODIS shutter logistics facilities
Third-party logistics provider Saddle Creek Corp. announced Nov. 19 that it will permanently close its facility in Groveport, Ohio, eliminating 150 jobs.
The layoffs are scheduled to begin Jan. 15.
Global logistics provider GEODIS also scheduled the permanent closure of an operation in Reno, Nevada, affecting 99 employees.
GEODIS filed its WARN notice Sept. 23, with the closure effective Nov. 22, just four days before Thanksgiving.
Morgan Truck Body closing Ohio manufacturing plant
Morgan Truck Body LLC is permanently closing its manufacturing plant in Orrville, Ohio, eliminating 73 jobs.
The company cited “unforeseeable business circumstances” in a WARN notice dated Nov. 18.
Morgan Truck Body manufactures commercial truck bodies used in freight transportation, distribution and last-mile delivery operations.
Packaging manufacturers eliminate nearly 100 jobs
Two packaging manufacturers are shuttering facilities in Pennsylvania and Missouri, eliminating a combined 96 positions.
J.L. Clark, a manufacturer of metal and plastic packaging products, plans to permanently close its facility in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, affecting 34 employees. The closure and layoffs are expected to be finalized in 2027.
Gateway Packaging Co. announced in a Nov. 20 notice that it will close its facility at 5910 Winner Road in Kansas City, Missouri.
The closure will leave 62 employees without jobs by Dec. 30, between Christmas and New Year’s Day.
Pepsi, Niagara Bottling closing production facilities
Workforce reductions are also affecting the beverage manufacturing sector.
Pepsi Bottling Group plans to permanently close its facility at 2708 Federal Road in Knoxville, Tennessee, eliminating 112 jobs effective Jan. 1.
The company notified the Tennessee Department of Labor and Workforce Development of the closure Oct. 19.
Niagara Bottling is also closing its water bottling plant in Ocala, Florida, affecting 57 employees. The layoffs are expected to be completed by the end of 2026.

1000-HP Ford GT Used in the Gran Turismo Movie Is Up for Grabs
9 photos
Photo: Car & Classic
By its nature, the Ford GT is, and it will probably forever be, one of the most sought-after vehicles in the collectors' world. I mean, first and foremost, the GTs from the first generation, produced by the Blue Oval as a tribute to the legendary GT40 in the mid-2000s.
History notes that, over the course of just a couple of years, just around 4,000 of these mid-engine two-seater sports cars have been made. That's few enough to make them extremely valuable, yet enough to make it impossible to keep track of them all.
That means nobody has an exact idea of what happened to all GTs made in 2005 and 2006. Some are most likely hidden in private collections, others occasionally show up for sale at various auctions, and we even know of one of them being declared a write-off before Galpin saved it and turned it into the world's only GTR1 .
One of these 2005 Ford GTs somehow landed a role in the 'Gran Turismo' movie released three years ago. The flick was not about the GT, but about the true story of a gamer with an inclination for racing games who turned into a professional driver with help from Nissan's GT Academy.
The role of the Ford GT in this flick was a relatively minor one, as it only appeared as one of the cars of choice for Kazunori Yamauchi, the creator of the Gran Turismo video game, played in the movie by Takehiro Hira. Painted black with the almost mandatory stripes on, the GT is seen in the opening sequences of the flick.
To the one who owns this vehicle, even this minor shot at stardom could make the GT worth a lot of money. Especially seeing how this is not a normal GT , but one heavily modified by Heffner Performance.
This crew is responsible for a lot of changes made to the car's powertrain, including the fitting of twin ball-bearing turbochargers, an air-to-water intercooler, a billet throttle body, and an upgraded fuel system.
Even the exhaust system has changed, enough for the original 5.4-liter V8 to jump from its stock 550 horsepower and 500 pound-feet of torque to about double that, 1,000 hp and 1,173 Nm of torque.
As one of the most powerful road-legal Ford GTs out there, the car only traveled a total of 12,000 miles (19,300 km) since it rolled off the lines, including for the needs of the movie it starred in.
I brought up this particular GT after I learned it is going to sell in an online auction by Car & Classic at the beginning of December 2026. There is no mention of how much it is expected to fetch, but we'll keep an eye on it and report back once we know more.

Mate Rimac Says the Tourbillon Is Only the Start of Bugatti's New Modular Platform
61 photos
Photo: Bugatti
Replacing a quad-turbo W16 monster developed from the Piech-era Veyron, the Tourbillon packs an 8.3-liter naturally aspirated V16 developed by Cosworth, three electric motors developed with Rimac know-how, and no fewer than 1,775 mechanical horsepower at full chatter. That number alone makes the Tourbillon a very interesting hypercar.
If you ask me, choosing a free-breathing engine this large and with this many cylinders is what sets the Bugatti apart from everything else in this segment. Sold out in its entirety, the Tourbillon coupe will gain at least one platform sibling in the next years and into the 2030s.
Speaking to Classic Drive, the big kahuna at Bugatti made it clear the Tourbillon's modularity gives the French automaker sufficient room to come up with different products. Mate Rimac refused to name Bugatti's planned future models. "I will stop here because my team will kill me otherwise," said the chief executive and technology officer at Bugatti Rimac.
Interestingly, he referred to the current Tourbillon as the "Tourbillon coupe" during the Classic Driver Talk interview. This alone suggests an open-top version of the plug-in hybrid V16-powered hypercar, and everyone would like that kind of Bugatti. In a similar fashion to the Lamborghini Revuelto and Temerario, the Bug features a mid-engine design with a rear-mounted electric motor and two electric drive units for the front axle.
Photo: Bugatti A high-voltage battery developed by Rimac sits in the middle, shaped into a T. The dual-clutch tranny of the Tourbillon sits behind the V16, and the fuel tanks were moved to the sides to create sufficient room for the rear end's underbody aero trickery. Each decision affected another part of the vehicle, yet the platform is still described as being highly modular.
Mate further revealed that Bugatti has a clear 10-year plan. Because it's no longer connected to the Volkswagen Group, the French company now has all the independence needed to make its own decisions, future product planning included. Mate talked about pursuing different directions and accepting risks larger organizations might struggle to approve, and this alone is very interesting.
How come? The Tourbillon itself emerged from a fight with the Volkswagen Group over whether Bugatti should build an electric SUV , a Chiron-derived hybrid, or something entirely new. Thankfully, the latter outcome gave us an exquisite V16 screamer. Although Mate did not say it during the interview, chances are that a four- or five-seat vehicle may be planned on this platform.
Photo: Bugatti He further mentioned a personal ambition to build a car weighing around 1,000 kilograms (2,205 pounds), which is Mazda MX-5 territory. The Roadster-branded model is currently listed at 1,010 kilograms (2,227 pounds) for the soft top with the 1.5-liter engine. By comparison, the Tourbillon coupe is advertised with less than 1,995 kilograms (4,398 pounds). 252 of those kilograms, namely 556 pounds, represent the weight of the Cosworth engine.
In any case, said personal ambition would give customers a way more direct and analog driving experience. Mate explicitly said that a lightweight model on the Tourbillon's platform is not something Bugatti is working on, so yeah, wishful thinking is all we've got for the time being.
As it stands, the Tourbillon coupe is the only application of the new modular platform. Its modularity should be viewed as a statement about engineering options, and the product roadmap is certain to be influenced by all commercially viable possibilities offered by its modularity.

View of ValOre's Pedra Branca property in Brazil. Credit: ValOre Metals.
Posted By: FREDERIC TOMESCO November 25, 2026
Canadian developer ValOre Metals (TSXV: VO; US-OTC: KVLQF) agreed to buy the Água Azul gold project in Brazil for $135 million (C$193 million) — more than 20 times the company’s market value before trading was halted Tuesday.
Vancouver-based ValOre plans to buy Bemisa Água Azul Mineração and an associated landholding entity from the Opportunity Holding investment fund, according to a statement Tuesday. The agreement will require a $90 million payment at closing, followed by $20 million after one year and $25 million after two years, subject to adjustments.
ValOre, which still needs to secure acquisition funding, expects the deal to close by Jan. 15, subject to TSX Venture Exchange acceptance. “Advanced” financing discussions covering the purchase, working capital and initial development spending are ongoing, the company said.
Under the agreement, ValOre has a one-time option within four months of closing to settle all $45 million of deferred payments for $30 million, subject to United States inflation adjustments. Exercising it would cut the nominal purchase price to $120 million.
Operating asset
Located about 1,900 km northwest of Sao Paulo, Água Azul would give ValOre a second Brazilian property, as well as a first operating asset. The company is already developing the Pedra Branca platinum group elements project in Ceará state, about 200 km from Fortaleza. Água Azul includes a 206-sq.-km land package that hosts the Abelhas, Juliano and Campos Altos deposit areas along a 15-km structural trend. Its Abelhas open-pit gold mine feeds a plant processing about 120,000 tonnes of material a year.
A July 28 preliminary economic assessment evaluates increasing the plant’s processing capacity to 2.85 million tonnes a year, following a three-year development period.
The study estimates $297 million in initial capital, including plant expansion, pre-stripping and contingency. At a 5% discount rate and a long-term gold price of $3,609 per oz., it calculates an after-tax net present value of $927.6 million and a 48% internal rate of return.
Mine schedule
Água Azul’s mine schedule spans 13 years, including about a decade at the expanded capacity. Estimated all-in sustaining costs are $1,540 per ounce. The assessment is preliminary and includes inferred resources, which are too speculative to support mineral reserves.
The property holds 22.8 million indicated tonnes grading 1.27 grams per tonne gold containing 931,920 oz. gold, according to a July resource. Inferred resources were estimated at 26.4 million tonnes grading 1.29 grams gold for contained metal of 1.1 million oz. gold.
The acquisition comes as ValOre advances processing research at Pedra Branca. On Nov. 10, it announced a five-year cooperation agreement with Germany’s federal geoscience institute and mineral resources agency through the government-funded BioPlat research project.
Shares of ValOre were halted Tuesday because the deal constitutes a fundamental acquisition under TSX Venture Exchange rules. They closed at 3.5¢ on Monday, valuing the company at C$8.9 million ($6.2 million).
ValOre expects the trading halt to last until closing.

A problem at a third-party manufacturer prompted Pharming to pause production of its cornerstone drug and warn that supply constraints are likely.
Pharming has paused production of its rare disease drug Ruconest in response to a simulation failure at its third-party fill-finish manufacturer.
The Dutch drugmaker warned that the temporary stoppage is likely to lead to supply constraints in the U.S. Pharming has enough Ruconest to serve the market through mid-December. The product is a C1 esterase inhibitor used to treat acute attacks in patients with hereditary angioedema (HAE). Ruconest stock held by specialty pharmacies and patients is unaffected.
Longer-term product availability will depend on the release of finished inventory and the completion of an investigation, which is looking into the root cause of the problem. Pharming will restart production once its partner has fixed the root cause and successfully requalified the manufacturing process.
Pharming named the failure of a routine simulation of the aseptic manufacturing process as the trigger for the production pause. The simulation, which is known as a media fill, is a validation test that mimics sterile manufacturing. By using microbiological growth media rather than the product, manufacturers can check whether their procedures and equipment prevent microbial contamination.
The company is encouraging patients to consult with their physicians, who have access to alternatives to Ruconest. KalVista Pharmaceuticals, which Chiesi Group bought recently for $1.9 billion, won FDA approval for an oral rival to injectable Ruconest last year. The oral drug, Ekterly, is a plasma kallikrein inhibitor indicated for the treatment of acute HAE attacks.
Physicians also have access to a growing arsenal of prophylactic treatments for preventing HAE attacks. Last year, the FDA approved CSL Behring’s Factor XIIa inhibitor Andembry and Ionis Pharmaceuticals’ prekallikrein-directed antisense oligonucleotide Dawnzera .
The launches posed threats to Ruconest even before the manufacturing problem created a trigger for patients to consider alternatives. Noting the intense competition in its annual report, Pharming warned investors of the risk that Ruconest “may no longer be competitive and accepted by physicians, patients, payors and others in the medical community.”
Pharming relies heavily on Ruconest, sales of which increased 14% to $93.8 million in the third quarter, accounting for 80% of the company’s revenues. The U.S. market generates effectively all Ruconest sales. Pharming’s other products are unaffected by the production pause. The company’s shares were down 14.6% to €1.01 ($1.11) in afternoon trading in Amsterdam following the news.

18 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
Do classic pickups from a long-gone era still keep you up at night for whatever reason? We won’t judge if they do, and in fact, you have come to the right place.
That’s because the 1967 Chevrolet C10 pictured above could be yours, if you really want it. The vehicle has been fully restored, and packs a 355 ci V8 engine with a .030 overbore, as well as a new intake manifold, a four-barrel carburetor, and a dual exhaust system.
These are some of the mods, and they are definitely not the only ones, as the ride in question also benefits from 22-inch wheels, backed up by power brakes. Power steering is also on deck, and additional highlights included LED lighting units at both ends, a relocated fuel filler behind the left taillight, and a sliding rear window. Air conditioning, custom upholstery, and a new steering wheel are also mentioned in the ad.
According to the listing, which we will link toward the end of the story, this Chevrolet C10 features a three-speed automatic transmission that sends the undisclosed output and thrust to the rear wheels. The truck has a green and white paint finish on the outside, a brown and black interior, and seems to retain the original gauges, as well as other bits and bobs. The ad also speaks about the “relatively soft-riding coil spring and trailing-arm rear suspension” that was a thing on two-wheel drive models.
Photo: Cars&Bids So, what else should interested parties know about this old timer that has received a new lease on life, with a restomod vibe courtesy of some of the modifications mentioned above? Well, that there is no known flaws category in the listing, and that the selling dealer reportedly bought it earlier this year. That would be in May 2026, and so far, they have added some 450 miles (725 km). The five-digit odometer reads 27,700 miles (44,600 km), and the real mileage is obviously unknown.
The Chevy C10 in question has a clean Indiana title, is currently located in Skokie, Illinois, and is accompanied by the keys and the owner’s manual. It is worth noting that classic rides may not carry emissions equipment, and that exemptions to emissions and safety testing vary from one state to the other. Thus, it is the buyer’s responsibility to make sure that they can register this old timer in their state before placing a bid.
Speaking of the latter, this Chevy C10 is advertised on Cars&Bids as part of an ongoing online auction. At the time of writing, the highest bid was $10,000, and there were six days left in the auction. The gavel will hit the table on December 1, 2026, and those who want to check it out in more detail and place a bid can do that here on the quoted website.

Maritime decarbonisation costs will ultimately be passed on to cargo owners under the present structuring of the proposed IMO Net-Zero Framework, according to the Federal Maritime Commission’s (FMC) chair Laura Di Bella.
With industry leaders backing her assessment, Ms Di Bella said the competitive nature of shipping would see additional compliance expenses eventually fed through to cargo owners, with ongoing regulatory uncertainty already forcing costs up.
When asked precisely how much of the IMO Framework’s estimated cost – which could be anywhere from $50bn-$260bn – would be passed on to shippers, Ms Di Bella told The Loadstar, “a very large percentage of it”.
“Shippers are hit with so many pass-through expenses. We’re constantly looking at all of the ways to tamp down any sort of inflationary measures, be it fuel surcharges or any surcharges, but what makes us think that this isn’t going to be treated the same way?” she explained.
Managing director of OceanScore Albrecht Grell agreed that the financial burden would ultimately be shouldered by cargo owners, arguing that shipping companies would seek to recover additional expenses through their commercial arrangements.
“Shipping is highly competitive – any cost will eventually be passed on to the cargo owners,” Mr Grell told The Loadstar , before warning that the redistribution of costs will not affect all shipping companies equally.
He said those able to adapt more effectively to the changing regulatory and operational environment would be able to pass on a higher share of their compliance expenses, adding “the profit pool will not change but be redistributed within the industry”.
Similarly, zero44 co-founder and managing director Friederike Hesse told The Loadstar uncertainty surrounding the regulatory framework is itself creating additional costs for the industry, as companies factor potential risks into their commercial decisions.
“Uncertainty is a cost too, companies price in risk premiums, put their eggs in multiple baskets instead of focusing investments, add contractual buffers and spend more on legal and administrative work, and that ends up in freight rates,” Ms Hesse said.
She added that this financial burden is then distributed through charter contracts, with responsibility depending on which party controls the operational decisions affecting fuel consumption and emissions.
“Whoever controls speed, route and fuel consumption pays for the emissions. Under time charters that is usually the charterer; under voyage charters it is priced into the freight. Cargo owners and consumers pay their share through rates and surcharges.”
Reiterating that the cost of transitioning could be anywhere between $50bn-$260bn, Ms Di Bella said there were clear questions as to whether the infrastructure required for it had been properly accounted for in discussions surrounding the framework.
Pointing to an infrastructure study commissioned by the IMO in April, which Ms Di Bella said has not yet been completed, she called for clearer understanding of the investment required before moving ahead.
“There is no infrastructure to support many of these alternative fuels. LNG is probably the closest that we have. So, we need to know what is it going to cost to get there? And then we work backwards.”
But Ms Hesse warned delaying emissions reductions would not cut decarbonisation’s eventual costs and could make the transition more expensive by leaving companies with less time to prepare through investment in vessels, fuels and infrastructure.
“Postponing cuts now does not make them disappear, it means much steeper targets later, at a point when companies will not have had time to prepare through early investment in ships, fuels and infrastructure,” she added.

NIO says its energy arm, NIO Power, will operate more than 10,000 battery swap stations and manage over RMB 350 billion ($52 billion) worth of battery packs by 2030.
That’s more than double the swap network NIO runs in China today. And it comes from a company that already missed its last big swap station target.
NIO shared the targets today at NIO IN 2026, its annual technology event, held in Guangzhou to mark the company’s 12th anniversary. NIO Power also expects to deliver over 10 billion kWh of energy per year through charging and battery swapping by the end of the decade.
From 4,252 swap stations to 10,000
As of November 11, NIO had 4,252 battery swap stations in China, alongside 5,584 charging stations, according to the company’s latest network count.

Getting to 10,000 by 2030 means adding roughly 1,400 swap stations per year for four straight years. NIO added 679 in 2024 and 681 in 2025. So the new plan needs about double the company’s recent pace.
Even this year’s goal of “at least 1,000” new stations looks tight. NIO had 3,729 swap stations in February when it celebrated its 100 millionth swap, which means it has added just over 500 since then.
There’s also some history here. At its 2021 Power Day, NIO committed to more than 4,000 battery swap stations worldwide by the end of 2025 , with about 1,000 of them outside China. By February 2026, it had about 3,700, almost all of them in China.
The energy target is just as aggressive. NIO’s swap network had delivered 5.28 billion kWh in total by February, after roughly eight years of operation. The 2030 goal is nearly twice that every year, although it also counts NIO’s charging stations.
Who pays for $52 billion in batteries?
NIO’s swap network is tied to its Battery-as-a-Service (BaaS) model, where customers can buy the car without the pack and rent the battery instead. That means someone has to own a massive fleet of packs, both in customers’ cars and sitting charged in stations. NIO says it wants to manage more than $52 billion of them in four years.
For context, NIO reported total revenue of about $4.7 billion in Q2 2026.
NIO has been moving the heavy capital off its own books. Under deals like its agreement with Zhongan Energy to build 500 swap stations within a year, partners own the stations while NIO handles the technology and operations. NIO Power says it has now co-built more than 900 swap stations with partners.
The hardware is also getting better. NIO opened its first fifth-generation swap stations in August, and they’re the first to serve all three of its brands. That includes the compact firefly, which couldn’t use older stations because of its shorter wheelbase.
NIO CFO Stanley Qu, who also heads NIO Power, presented the unit as NIO’s showcase for running a business with AI agents, using them to manage battery value, station operations, and energy efficiency.
The rest of NIO IN: self-driving, NOMI, and “AI-native”
The swap targets were only part of the event; everything else focused on NIO’s AI-fication.
NIO also launched NIO WorldModel (NWM) 3.0, the latest version of its driver-assist AI, which starts rolling out in December to vehicles with the Banyan, Cedar, Cedar S, and Coconut+ systems, pending regulatory clearance.
NIO says NWM 3.0 needs 40% fewer driver interventions than the previous version. It didn’t say how many interventions it started from, which makes the number hard to evaluate. It also claims a roughly 60% boost in drivers’ “sense of reassurance,” whatever that means.
The more concrete claims are about speed: NIO says overall vehicle control latency is down 54% and chassis control latency is down 78%, while training is five times more efficient.
NIO also unveiled NOMI Intelligence 4.0, a rebuild of its in-car assistant around an AI agent framework that can plan and carry out tasks on its own instead of following set commands. The first release, Cedar 2.0.0, will be filed in early December. Cars on Cedar S and Banyan should get it in Q2 2027, followed later by ONVO models.
Finally, CEO William Li pitched NIO as an “AI-native organization.” He argued the global auto industry is worth $7 to $9 trillion and that AI could add more than $1.2 trillion in value to it. NIO says it has deployed over 7,500 AI agents internally, with more than 2.9 million executions so far.
Electrek’s Take
NIO’s swap network is real, and it works. The company passed 130 million swaps this month, and nobody else has built anything close at this scale. Tesla sort of tried battery swapping and quietly dropped it. NIO kept going.
But 10,000 stations by 2030 requires a build pace NIO has never hit, and its last swap target slipped badly. So we’d treat that number as an ambition, not a forecast.
The $52 billion battery figure is the interesting part. It shows what NIO Power really is: a battery asset manager that also builds stations. That only works if partners keep putting up the capital and the batteries keep earning money over their lifetime. NIO has been trying to get other automakers on board for years, with limited results – though it appears to be starting to attract more players.
And the competition isn’t standing still. Chinese automakers like BYD are pushing megawatt-level charging that adds hundreds of kilometers of range in about the time it takes to swap a battery. If ultra-fast charging becomes common, NIO’s swap advantage gets a lot thinner.
Battery swapping is one way to recharge in minutes, but if you drive an EV, charging at home on solar power is still the cheapest way to fuel it. Real versus nominal sales, the New York Fed’s K-shape claim, and what jobs, wages, and sentiment say about consumer strength
Retail and food services sales were $748.2 billion in October 2026, up 6.82% from a year earlier. Deflated by CPI, real sales were up an estimated 2.76% in October, about 4.4% above their April 2024 trough, despite CPI inflation of an estimated 3.95%, PPI inflation of 6.52%, and record-low University of Michigan sentiment (44.8 in May). Fuel is the main distortion: gas station sales were up 28% and diesel prices about 60%, moves large enough that a CPI deflator cannot cleanly separate price from volume. Gas stations supplied 32% of September’s dollar growth; excluding them, real growth was roughly 1% to 1.8%, a range that brackets the 1.6% pre-Covid pace. Other drivers are a saving rate that fell to 3.8% (5.1% a year earlier, 6.5% in 2017 to 2019), larger tax refunds, and wealth gains concentrated at the top, with credit a smaller factor. The New York Fed reads its income-group data as a K-shaped economy. Its own series show a one-time gap that opened in 2023 and parallel growth since 2024 (+7.3%, +6.5%, and +5.2% for low-, middle-, and high-income households through February 2026), which fits a slower low-income recovery from Covid better than a widening K. Jobs are stable but low-hire, and real wages and total compensation are flat. 2026 looks like a return to normal growth funded by a lower saving rate, not by rising purchasing power.

XV80 Toyota Camry Hybrid Produced in the United States Arrives in Japan After a Three-Year Hiatus
7 photos
Photo: Toyota
The latest Toyota Camry , now only a hybrid sedan in its latest XV80 interpretation, is coming home to Japan - via production units built in the US in Kentucky, as it turns out.
The story of the Toyota Camry nameplate is quite long and extensive – it was first a compact car launched internationally by the Japanese automaker since 1982, and the narrow-body model overlapped for a time with the wide-body version that entered the mid-size market in 1991.
Now it’s one of the best-selling sedans in the world, especially in America, where it found a home-away-from-home – the love affair has been just as long and arduous. The latest iteration came out in late 2023 at the Los Angeles Auto Show in California, and while it retained the same TNGA-K architecture as its predecessor, it has become a hybrid-only model in markets like North America and the Old Continent.
Well, now it’s time for the prodigal son to return home, as Toyota has now announced that the latest Camry, produced at the Kentucky plant in the United States, officially comes back to the Japanese market on December 23, 2026. Just in time to celebrate Christmas a little earlier, right?
Anyway, the Toyota Camry has been absent from its "home" market since 2023, and now it comes as the "Made in the US, Made by Toyota" Camry – as hinted back in June 2026 during the "North American Camry Custom Showdown" event that took place at the Super Taikyu (S-Tai) Fuji 24 Hours, where the Toyota Chairman Akio Toyoda (“affectionately known as Morizo”) explained the ongoing tariff issues might ease off if they sell the US-made Camry in Japan.
The eleventh-generation Toyota Camry thus returns to the Land of the Rising Sun with a US passport, “meticulously adapted for Japanese roads” with right-hand drive, right-sided turn signal switches, and a fully localized Japanese multimedia and navigation system.
Unlike the Toyota Tundra full-size pickup truck and the Toyota Highlander, which are sold in Japan via the bilateral framework agreement allowing the company to skip additional testing for US-certified vehicles, the Camry has been submitted to Japan’s Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism for official domestic vehicle type certification.
The Toyota Camry is said to be nearly identical in footprint to the Crown Signia crossover, but with a lower roofline, and will be available at home in Japan in two grades: Z and G, starting from ¥5,200,000 or $32,655 for the former and from ¥4,300,000 for the latter, which translates to just $27k at the current exchange rate. In the US, the cheapest 2027 Camry goes from $29,700 sans destination, so the JDM version is actually a sweeter deal for local residents.
Of course, it comes to Japan with the same 2.5L Series Parallel Hybrid System (A25A-FXS) boasting 225 combined horsepower – though it’s only available with front-wheel drive, not also AWD like in America.

Shein has agreed to pay $100 million to resolve Federal Trade Commission allegations that it failed to notify shoppers about late shipments and kept negative product reviews off its site. The agency also alleges the retailer misled shoppers about supplier audits and where some of its cotton was grown.
What’s Related
The FTC filed its complaint and proposed settlement Tuesday in federal court in California. The deal needs a judge’s approval. The agency would use the money to compensate affected customers.
A Shein spokesperson told The Associated Press that the agreement “does not constitute an admission of liability, and we continue to disagree with aspects of the FTC’s characterization of our business and compliance practices.”
What happens when an order ships late
The FTC says Shein ships nearly 1 million packages into the U.S. each day. According to the complaint, Shein told shoppers it would process and ship orders within one to three days and showed estimated delivery dates at checkout. Some shoppers waited weeks or more than a month for their orders to arrive, the agency alleges.
The FTC says Shein tracked delays across its carriers but repeatedly failed to give shoppers the choice federal rules require when orders can’t ship on time. Under the proposed order, Shein would have to notify affected shoppers within a reasonable time after learning of a delay and no later than the original ship date. Shoppers could accept the delay or cancel for a prompt refund.
RELATED: Shein Agrees to $100 Million Settlement Over Delivery Complaints
No audits to back up claims
Shein marketed its evoluSHEIN line as coming from suppliers that scored above average on audits designed to guard against child and forced labor . The FTC says the company provided no audit that backed up that claim.
Shein relied on supplier paperwork and third-party testing to trace where its cotton was grown. The FTC says testing pointed to China for some samples suppliers had identified as U.S.-grown. More than 7% of the samples Shein submitted lacked enough documentation to establish a country of origin, according to the complaint. The proposed order would require Shein to back up claims about supplier audits and its ability to trace cotton.
When packages went missing
The FTC says Shein marked packages as delivered if a photo showed a drop-off, without requiring proof that the package reached the correct address. When shoppers reported that they hadn’t received their packages, Shein directed them to the carrier or told them to dispute the charge with their bank, the agency says.
As of September 2025, Shein had just five agents handling calls from U.S. shoppers and didn’t list a customer service number on its website, the FTC says. “SHEIN further compounded consumer harm by making it extraordinarily difficult to obtain customer service,” said Christopher Mufarrige, director of the FTC’s Bureau of Consumer Protection.
The proposed order would require Shein to clearly post ways to reach customer service by phone and in writing. It would also limit when Shein could send customers to a carrier or bank to resolve a shipping dispute and bar it from blocking negative reviews.

What happens when an order ships late
According to the complaint, Shein told shoppers it would process and ship orders within one to three days and showed estimated delivery dates at checkout.
Some shoppers waited weeks or more than a month for their orders to arrive, the agency alleges.
The FTC says Shein tracked delays across its carriers but repeatedly failed to give shoppers the choice federal rules require when orders can’t ship on time.
Under the proposed order, Shein would have to notify affected shoppers within a reasonable time after learning of a delay and no later than the original ship date.
Shoppers could accept the delay or cancel for a prompt refund.

S&P Global Ratings raised its long-term issuer credit rating on Canadian Pacific Kansas City Ltd. (NYSE: CP) to A- from BBB+. It also raised the rating on the railroad’s unsecured debt to A- from BBB+.
S&P on Tuesday said CPKC has kept delivering solid results despite economic and trade headwinds, and noted a stable outlook. It said this shows the strength of the company’s diversity and growth opportunities after its acquisition of Kansas City Southern in 2023. The upgrade follows S&P’s December 2025 move to a positive outlook on the BBB+ rating.
Growth ahead of competitors
Since 2022, CPKC’s pro forma volumes, revenue and adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) have grown faster than those of the other North American Class 1 railroads, S&P said. It expects that to continue. The agency credited the KCS merger and subsequent integration, and service improvements. It also credited the only single-line rail network linking Canada, the United States and Mexico.
S&P expects volumes to rise by a low-single-digit percentage on truck-to-rail conversion on U.S.-Mexico lanes; intermodal partnerships with Maersk (OTC: AMKBY )-Hapag-Lloyd’s ( HLAG.DE ) Gemini cooperation, Schneider National (NYSE: SNDR ) and Americold (NYSE: COLD ); and coal volumes recovered from Elk Valley Resources, business CPKC lost to Canadian National (NYSE: CNI ) in 2021.
S&P said these gains should more than offset tougher Canadian grain comparisons, as well as competitive pressure from a potential Union Pacific (NYSE: UNP )–Norfolk Southern (NYSE: NSC ) merger.
Year to date through Nov. 21, revenue ton miles were up about 4.2%. Grain, minerals and consumer products offset flat or falling industrial volumes. About 41% of revenue comes from goods crossing the Canada-U.S. or Mexico-U.S. border. Even so, S&P expects tariffs to cut revenue by less than 1% this year. Tariff-exposed lanes make up under 20% of freight revenue.
Financial forecasts
S&P expects the following indicators to develop over the next few years:
Adjusted funds from operations (FFO) to debt of 23%–25%
Adjusted debt to EBITDA of 2.8x–3.0x
Mid-single-digit annual EBITDA growth
Capital spending of 16%–17% of revenue
Annual free operating cash flow of C$3.5–C$4 billion ($2.46-2.81 billion), or 12%–15% of debt
Net leverage was 3.2x at Sept. 30, 2026. S&P expects it to reach management’s 2.75x target by the end of next year. It also expects CPKC to spend at least $1.76 billion a year on buybacks and raise dividends about 10% a year, adjusting buybacks to stay near the leverage target.
What could change the rating
S&P warned it could downgrade CPKC within 24 months if FFO to debt falls below 23% or free operating cash flow to debt falls below 10% on a sustained basis. That could follow a more aggressive financial policy or weaker operations. An upgrade would need sustained FFO to debt above 35% and free operating cash flow to debt above 18%, along with more conservative financial policies.
CP shares closed Nov. 24 at $92.82, up 2.42%. Its market capitalization is about $80.7 billion. The stock has traded between $70.01 and $96.90 over the past 52 weeks.
Analyst sentiment on the company is bullish. Of eight ratings tracked, six are bullish and two neutral, with none bearish. The average price target is about $111.38, and the median is $103. Targets range from $93 to $145.
Why It Matters: A higher credit rating usually lowers borrowing costs and widens the pool of investors who can hold a company’s debt. It signals that a rating agency sees the post-merger railroad as financially stronger and more resilient, even with trade uncertainty.
